study type: Secondary analysis of an observational study
exposure: Mode of delivery (induction of labor vs. prelabor cesarean delivery)
Gestational age at delivery (24(0)-28(6) weeks vs. 29(0)-<33(0) weeks)
gestational age at delivery (23(0) and <33(0) weeks' gestation)
cohort: 471 patients with pregnancy-associated hypertension (gestational hypertension or preeclampsia) delivered between 23(0) and <33(0) weeks' gestation
finding: Labor induction, compared to prelabor cesarean delivery in patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy before 33 weeks' gestation, was associated with significantly lower odds of maternal morbidity but not neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: More than half of the patients (53%) who underwent labor induction had a vaginal delivery.
